<tool-use data-tool-type="unknown" data-tool-name="create_plan"><details>

Parameters:

````json
{
  "name": "Attendance status table",
  "overview": "`dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance_status` is not created by Spark. It is a dbt semantic Iceberg table rebuilt by the `saal_model` Airflow DAG from `int_attendance_day` for one reporting month.",
  "plan": "# How `employee_attendance_status` is created\n\nThe Iceberg table `dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance_status` is created by **dbt**, not by Spark. Spark jobs only land source data in `raw.employee`.\n\n## Where it is defined\n\n[`saal-data-model/models/semantic/employee_attendance_status.sql`](saal-data-model/models/semantic/employee_attendance_status.sql) materializes a **table** with:\n\n- `database='dataproducts'`\n- `schema='employee'`\n- `on_table_exists='drop'` (full rebuild: drop then create each run)\n\nThat matches [`dbt_project.yml`](saal-data-model/dbt_project.yml): semantic models go to `dataproducts.employee` as Iceberg tables.\n\nOn every dbt run, [`ensure_iceberg_schema`](saal-data-model/macros/ensure_iceberg_schema.sql) runs first so `dataproducts.employee` exists. dbt-trino then `CREATE TABLE` from the SELECT (drop if the table already exists).\n\nThere is no Spark `CREATE TABLE` / write for this name. Related history is a different model: [`employee_attendance_status_history.sql`](saal-data-model/models/semantic/employee_attendance_status_history.sql) (`incremental`).\n\n## Pipeline that builds it\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  sparkJobs[\"Spark DAGs: employee_data, leave, onsite\"]\n  rawIceberg[\"raw.employee Iceberg\"]\n  airflow[\"Airflow DAG saal_model\"]\n  dbtStaging[\"dbt staging views\"]\n  dbtInt[\"dbt intermediate tables\"]\n  statusTable[\"dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance_status\"]\n\n  sparkJobs --\u003e rawIceberg\n  airflow --\u003e dbtStaging\n  rawIceberg --\u003e dbtStaging\n  dbtStaging --\u003e dbtInt\n  dbtInt --\u003e statusTable\n```\n\n[`saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py`](saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py) runs:\n\n1. `dbt run --select path:models/staging/employee`\n2. `dbt run --select path:models/intermediate`\n3. `dbt run --select path:models/semantic` — this is the step that creates the table\n4. `dbt test` including `employee_attendance_status`\n\ndbt talks to Trino (LDAP via `TRINO_*` env vars in [`profiles.yml`](saal-data-model/profiles.yml)).\n\n## What the SQL does\n\n1. **Month filter** via [`attendance_reporting_bounds()`](saal-data-model/macros/attendance_reporting_bounds.sql): `attendance_year` + `attendance_month` if set, otherwise the **previous calendar month**.\n2. Reads [`int_attendance_day`](saal-data-model/models/intermediate/int_attendance_day.sql) (office + onsite + leave, HR overlay).\n3. Nulls `LastPunch` when there is one punch or first/last share the same `HH:mm`.\n4. Sets `PunchStatus` / `AttendanceStatus` (leave, half-day at 13:00, unauthorized half-day, Present).\n5. Outputs reporting columns (`EmployeeID`, `Date` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, punch times as `HH:mm`, `TotalHoursInOffice`, etc.).\n\nGrain: one row per `coalesce(BusinessEmail, EmployeeID) + Date` (documented in [`_semantic__models.yml`](saal-data-model/models/semantic/_semantic__models.yml)).\n\n## Upstream of `int_attendance_day`\n\nStaging views over `raw.employee` ([`sources.yml`](saal-data-model/models/staging/sources.yml)):\n\n- `employee_attendance_metrics` (iClock punches)\n- `onsite_employee`\n- `leave_data`\n- `employee_hr_data`\n\nThose become `int_office_day`, `int_onsite_day`, `int_leave_day`, then `int_attendance_day` in `dataproducts.employee_model`.\n\n## What this is not\n\n- Not created by [`employee_data`](employee_data) Spark scripts.\n- Rebuilds **one month only**; long history is `employee_attendance_status_history`.\n"
}
````

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Only leave people show up because **the status table is not leave-only by design**. It is a full outer join of office, onsite, and leave, then **kept for one reporting month**. Punch-only people disappear when that month has **no office/onsite days**, while leave still has days in that month.

That happens because the three Spark current tables are not the same kind of snapshot:

- **Leave:** Spark overwrites `raw.employee.leave_data` with the **whole Excel**. dbt then expands every day from `leave_from_date` to `leave_to_date`. A YTD (or multi-month) file still produces days in August (or whatever month `saal_model` used).
- **Office / onsite:** Spark **replaces** `employee_attendance_metrics` and `onsite_employee` with **one month**.
- **Status:** [`employee_attendance_status.sql`](saal-data-model/models/semantic/employee_attendance_status.sql) then keeps only `attendance_year` / `attendance_month` (or the previous Dubai calendar month). Default now is **August 2026**.

If iClock or onsite last ran for **September** (or another month), those punch dates fall outside the window and are dropped. Leave days that fall in August stay. You are left with people who have leave, and nobody who only punched.

A person-key mismatch (office keyed by emp id, leave by email) can **split** punch vs leave into two rows. It does **not** drop punch-only people. Missing punch-only people means `int_office_day` / `int_onsite_day` are empty or outside that month.

Check in Trino:

```sql
select min("Date"), max("Date"), count(*)
from dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance_status;

select 'office' src, min(attendance_date), max(attendance_date), count(*)
from dataproducts.employee_model.int_office_day
union all
select 'onsite', min(attendance_date), max(attendance_date), count(*)
from dataproducts.employee_model.int_onsite_day
union all
select 'leave', min(attendance_date), max(attendance_date), count(*)
from dataproducts.employee_model.int_leave_day;
```

If office/onsite dates are not in the same month as status `Date`, re-run iClock and onsite for that month, then `saal_model` with the same year/month. Current status does not read `*_history`; that is a different table.

---

leave	2026-04-24T00:00:00	2026-12-31T00:00:00	783
office	2026-08-03T00:00:00	2026-08-31T00:00:00	1236
onsite	2026-08-01T00:00:00	2026-08-31T00:00:00	372

**The problem**

Airflow is running an old copy of the DAG file. During the July backfill, someone temporarily hardcoded July 2026 into `saal_model.py`. That hardcode was later removed from this repo, but the copy sitting at `/opt/airflow/dags/saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py` on the worker was never updated.

Your run from today proves it. The log printed `TEMP hardcoded reporting period: 2026-07` — a line that exists nowhere in this repo — and passed `{"attendance_year": 2026, "attendance_month": 7}` to dbt. So dbt rebuilt July again, 138 rows.

July has 138 leave days and zero punch days, because your office and onsite raw tables were overwritten with **August** data (1236 and 372 rows). Leave looks like the only thing in the table because leave ranges get expanded day by day across April–December, so July still has leave rows to show. The table isn't filtering to leave; July just has nothing else in it.

The reason the September logical_date trick didn't work is that the month never comes from the run date on that deployed file — it's pinned in the code.

**What to do**

1. Copy this repo's `saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py` over the deployed one on the Airflow scheduler and every worker.
2. Verify the hardcode is gone: `grep -n "TEMP hardcoded" /opt/airflow/dags/saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py` should print nothing.
3. Wait for Airflow to re-parse the DAG, then trigger `saal_model` with a logical_date in September (today works — manual runs use the previous month in Dubai time).
4. In the `dbt-run-semantic` log, confirm `"attendance_month": 8` and that `employee_attendance_status` was created with well over 138 rows.

You don't need to re-run any Spark job for this. August punches are already in `int_office_day` and `int_onsite_day`.

**One caution**

The same July hardcode was also put into `leave_data.py`, `onsite_employee.py`, and `employee_data.py`. Those are clean here, but the copies in MinIO might not be. If you trigger `employee_data` or `onsite_employee` before re-running `deploy_pipeline.sh`, a stale script would overwrite your August raw punches back to July and put you right back where you started.
